column1: # Cedar Rapids case data, and where every byte came from.
# Two USGS data releases, both public and both re-fetchable from the DOI. Files
# are renamed for legibility where the release's own names are long; the
# original name is recorded, because a renamed file that cannot be matched back
# to its delivery is a file with no provenance.
# Nothing here is derived. Where a later stage crops or converts one of these,
# it says so in the file it writes and in docs/case2_cedar_rapids.md.

column4: Edwards CW3: dipole-dipole, Schlumberger, inverse Schlumberger, and a combined file.
Ellis CW1, as three nested zips one per array. Its README endpoints span 477 m against a 275 m electrode line; trust the electrodes.
Seminole Valley Park CW6: dipole-dipole and inverse Schlumberger. No Schlumberger, though the metadata says three arrays everywhere.
Seminole Valley Park S10: dipole-dipole and inverse Schlumberger. No Schlumberger.
Seminole Valley Park demonstration line: all three arrays.
The release's own note. Documents the .stg, .crs and .cmd formats field by field, and gives each site's endpoints.
FGDC metadata. States 15 surveys; 13 are present.
139,602 RESOLVE soundings, six frequencies, in-phase and quadrature in ppm, plus magnetics and altimetry. What this case inverts.
The contractor's EM1DFM inversion, 28 layers per sounding with a depth of investigation. The independent check.
Defines every column of both CSVs.
CGG's survey and processing report. The source for the system, the frequencies and the calibration.
FGDC metadata for the AEM release.
Borehole NMR, natural gamma and induction, June 2017. Inside the model volume. 18.4 m deep, does not reach rock.
Inside the model volume. No bedrock pick in the text layer.
Inside the model volume. Its lithology column names limestone, but the depth is drawn rather than written.
Inside the model volume, and the only one with a numeric bedrock pick: shaley limestone at 55 ft below a casing top 0.73 m above ground, so 16.0 m below ground.
FGDC metadata for the borehole geophysics. Five further wells sit outside the volume and were not fetched.
